findings.F1: Hourly returns between 20:00 and 22:00 UTC beat the coin's mean hourly return in both coins. Hour 20 averages +0.045 % (t 4.00) and hour 21 +0.040 % (t 3.69), about 5,840 hours each. These are the only two of 24 hours with a t above 3, so they stand out even after testing every hour. Pooled over both hours, BTC averages +0.037 % (t 3.81, 5,837 hours) and ETH +0.048 % (t 3.92, 5,837 hours).
findings.F2: The 20–22 UTC excess return holds outside any one period. It is positive in 7 of 8 years: from +0.028 % to +0.077 %, with t 1.2 to 3.7. The exception is 2022, at −0.031 % (t −1.45). It is positive on all 7 weekdays: from +0.034 % to +0.053 %, with t 1.5 to 2.8.
findings.F3: The 20–22 UTC excess return is largest after the coin fell over the prior 24 hours. By quartile of the prior 24-hour return it is +0.093 % (t 4.41) in the lowest quartile, +0.035 % (t 3.01) in the second, +0.003 % (t 0.22) in the third and +0.042 % (t 2.46) in the highest. The grading is clear across the lower three quartiles and breaks in the top one.
findings.F4: The opposite holds around the start of the UTC day. Hour 2 averages −0.032 % (t −3.35), hour 1 −0.023 % (t −2.22) and hour 0 −0.023 % (t −1.97). Only hour 2 clears the bar for 24 hours tested.

ideas.idea: Each coin rises more than its usual hourly drift over the 20:00–22:00 UTC hours. The further the coin fell over the past 24 hours, the larger that rise.
ideas.consequence: A trader would lean long into the 20–22 UTC hours, more after a falling day, and avoid opening shorts just before them. Each hour adds only about 0.04–0.09 %, so this works as a timing tilt on existing trades, not as a stand-alone trade against a 0.11 % round-trip cost.
ideas.name: late-US hours rebound rise

ideas.idea: Each coin falls more than its usual hourly drift over the 00:00–03:00 UTC hours. The larger its rise over the preceding 20:00–00:00 UTC hours, the larger that fall.
ideas.consequence: A trader would avoid entering longs just after midnight UTC and would time exits of long trades before those hours rather than after.
ideas.name: early-UTC hours give back
